q: Phosphofructokinase, an early enzyme of glycolysis, is inhibited by high ATP and activated by high ADP/AMP. What does this show about respiration as a system?
options: Respiration is controlled by positive feedback, so ATP production keeps accelerating once it starts
ATP output is regulated by negative feedback, matching the rate of respiration to energy demand
Glycolysis can only take place once all the ATP in the cell has been completely used up
ATP is the only substrate of phosphofructokinase, so more ATP always speeds glycolysis up
explanation: When ATP is plentiful it binds an allosteric site on phosphofructokinase and slows glycolysis – end-product (negative feedback) inhibition. As ATP is used and ADP/AMP rise, the enzyme is activated and respiration speeds up. This self-regulation is a property of respiration as a system: ATP supply tracks demand without wasting substrate.
